incident-bot: PagerDuty: INC12345 fired for service=pg-client-proxy (high pg connections) :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Triggered by policy 'db-conn-threshold' — urgency: high — runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/db-conn
maria: acked oncall — looking
kevin: I'm jumping in, grabbing connection metrics now
maria: thanks. any customer-facing alerts yet? sam, can you check Support?
sam: no active public incidents from support console, one ticket from ACME complaining about 502s ~2m ago
kevin: seeing accept queue growing on pgbouncer hosts -> `stats` show `cl_active` ~ 420, max configured 500 but tail latency spiking
kevin: also seeing increased `waiting_clients` on read-replicas, looks like connection churn, not steady increase
maria: is this correlated with a deploy? deploy-bot: No deploys in last 30m
jamie: PagerDuty escalations may start if not acked by next rotation. Maria, if you want to handoff, say so
maria: handing to kevin, i'm tied up with another customer call — handoff acknowledged @kevin
kevin: thanks. initial mitigation: enable emergency circuit breaker to reject new api clients for non-critical routes. Pushing policy via infra-automation-bot
infra-automation-bot: Applying traffic policy `circuit-breaker/read-heavy` to route `openapi.v1.embed` — rollout 25%
kevin: also temporarily increase pgbouncer `max_client_conn` on proxy pool B to 800 to drain backlog (will monitor CPU)
kevin: command I ran on proxy-b-1:
```
sudo systemctl restart pgbouncer && pgbouncerctl show stats | grep wait
```
kevin: note: restart may drop some idle connections, expected
maria: what's the customer impact window? sam?
sam: ACME ticket shows 502s starting 00:01:10 UTC, about 3 minutes ago, estimate affected cohort ~2% of live traffic (ingest-heavy customers)
kevin: rolling the pgbouncer increase now across B pool
infra-automation-bot: pgbouncer max_client_conn updated on proxy-b-1, proxy-b-2, proxy-b-3
kevin: accept queue decreasing, `cl_active` now 260 on b-1, tail p95 latency down from 1.8s to 420ms
maria: nice. can we throttle non-essential background jobs?
kevin: yes, placing dedupe and analytics ingestion to low priority — scaling down ingestion workers by 40%:
```
kubectl scale deployment ingestion-workers --replicas=6 -n prod
```
kevin: doing that now
infra-automation-bot: scaled ingestion-workers -> replicas=6
kevin: waiting 30s for in-flight jobs to drain
maria: coordinating customer comms: @sam please post a minimal status update: investigating DB connection saturation causing intermittent 502s, mitigation in progress
sam: Posted: "We're investigating increased database connection load causing intermittent errors for a small subset of customers. Mitigation underway, updates in 15m." :thumbsup:
kevin: monitoring… accept queue steady ~120, p95 latency ~380ms, no new PD alerts so far
maria: good. any sign of underlying postgres process saturation?
kevin: cpu on primary spiked to 85% briefly but queries look normal; suspect application burst (retry storm) hitting connection pool limits. also saw many short-lived connections from a particular client key
kevin: running a quick query to identify offending client:
```
SELECT client_addr, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state!='idle' GROUP BY client_addr ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5;
```
kevin: found ~320 ephemeral connections from 10.9.22.18 — that's a mobile backend that rolled traffic. emailing eng contact to throttle
maria: can we add a prefix cache/KV short-term to reduce DB hits for those requests? jamie, any thoughts on quick wins?
jamie: short-term: increase pooling and add 30s prefix cache at edge for the problematic route; medium-term: recommend adding client-side retry jitter and connection pooling rules
kevin: applied edge cache via CDN edge rule for route `/v1/records/fetch`: cache-control 30s
infra-automation-bot: CDN rule applied to edge cluster us-east-1
maria: monitoring metrics and PD status. if we hold steady 15m, i'll close the PD loop and create follow-up ticket for hardening & client outreach
kevin: still seeing small tail of retries but overall throughput down 28% and errors trending to 0.5% from 3.2%
sam: support noted ACME responded to update and is monitoring on their end
maria: ok, starting post-incident notes in #postmortems after we stabilize — please capture commands and timestamps
kevin: will add a snippet of the query and pgbouncer changes to the incident doc
incident-bot: PagerDuty: INC12345 acknowledged by kevin at 5222223335 — escalation stopped
maria: leaving handback to kevin for final remediation and RCA
kevin: plan: 1) contact offending client to add pooling, 2) tighten server-side per-client connection caps, 3) add automatic autosquelch for sudden client spikes, 4) run a tabletop next week. I'll open tickets
maria: thanks all — good remediation work. keeping channel open for 30m housekeeping
sam: will follow up with ACME once we close out
kevin: closing actions created: RED-789 (client contact), RED-790 (autosquelch), RED-791 (pgbouncer tuning). assigning owners
maria: resolved for now, will update #postmortems when RCA is drafted :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident INC12345 marked resolved at 5222223599
